newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end slightly lower.

text.p: U.S. debt futures closed slightly lower, but traders are looking for March T-bonds to rise in the near- to intermediate-term.
"The market looks in good shape to rise to 113-26/32 to 114-06/32," one bond market analyst said.
While activity was light in the pit, traders noted good buying in the cash bond market.
"Fundamentally, the market is absorbing a lot of supply," he added. "Demand is overwhelming supply."
Several analysts said demand from corporate pension funds and overseas investors was strong.
As a result, they said the U.S. Treasury's announcement of a $39.75 billion note and bond auction had little affect on the market.
One trader said the strength in the dollar was fueling foreign demand for U.S. assets.
"U.S. yields denominated in dollars is a good deal," one trader said. "Where else do you go if you are a foreign investor."
He said U.S. yields were also attractive for domestic investors.
"A 6.50 to 7.0 percent yield on the 30-year bond is well valued," he said.

Traders had little reaction to the Federal Open Market Committee's decision to leave rates unchanged, but they attributed the listless pace of activity on the floor to lingering concerns about the outcome of the meeting.
Aside from several large firms each selling about 3,000 to 4,000 March T-bonds, order flow was light.
Traders are now focusing on the January employment data, which will be released on Friday at 0830 EST/1330 GMT. U.S. weekly jobless claims will be released on Thursday.
Jobless claims for the week ended February 1 are expected to fall to 347,000, from 351,000 in the prior week.

At the end of pit trade, March T-bonds were off 06/32 at 112-01/32, 10-year notes were down 02/32 at 109-05/32, March T-bills were steady at 94.96, June Eurodollars were also unchanged at 94.31 and September Eurodollars were one basis point lower at 94.17.
